title: Accelerated weathering and oxidative degradation alter the surface chemistry, morphology and charge properties of PET microplastic fibres
content: Microplastic fibres released from synthetic textiles are a major source of plastic contamination in wastewater treatment systems and agricultural soils receiving biosolids. Understanding how these fibres transform during environmental ageing is important for evaluating their environmental fate and potential interactions with co-occurring contaminants. This study investigated the physicochemical transformation of cryomilled polyethylene terephthalate (PET) microplastic fibres (MPFs) subjected to accelerated weathering and oxidative degradation using multiple analytical techniques. The fibres exhibited dimensions (183 ± 159 µm length; 20.6 ± 3.6 µm width) comparable to those reported for textile-derived microplastic fibres. Both ageing processes induced substantial changes in fibre properties, including increased surface roughness, cracking and fragmentation, a four-fold increase in surface area (0.045 ± 0.005–0.187 ± 0.004 m2 g−1), reduced thermal stability, and changes in PET surface chemistry consistent with oxidative modification. Changes in surface charge were also observed, with the point of zero charge (pHPZC) decreasing from 5.02 to 3.03, indicating increased surface acidity following degradation. These transformations suggest that PET MPFs subjected to accelerated weathering and oxidative degradation may exhibit different environmental behaviour from pristine fibres due to changes in surface morphology, chemistry and charge. The results highlight the importance of considering degraded induced physicochemical changes when evaluating the potential environmental behaviour of PET MPFs and provide a basis for future investigations of their environmental fate and interactions with co-occurring contaminants.
